title: LP1 column balance after searching section orders
question: How unusual is the flattest arrangement after searching all 24 orders of the four intact LP1 sections?
summary: All 24 orders form six cyclic classes. The original arrangement remains tied for best; matching the order search in every shuffled control gives a plus-one estimate of 0.00882.

scope.representation: Archived ciphertext runes, headings and interrupting F retained. Join slash and newline wraps and consecutive pages within a section. Rune runs with internal apostrophes form one word; apostrophes count zero runes. Other non-runes delimit words. Never merge sections.
scope.procedure: Retain all 464 word lengths and continuous 29-by-16 layout. Search all 24 orders of the four intact sections and retain minimum Q. In each control shuffle lengths within sections, search the same 24 orders, and retain its minimum.
scope.parameters: 16 columns; section sizes 45,124,208,87; all 24 orders represented by six cyclic classes; 49,999 trials; Python random.Random seed 330146; lower tail including ties; (tail_count+1)/50000; threshold 0.05. Earlier fixed-order results known before this protocol.
scope.exclusions: Other widths, reversals, sentence removal, sentence-preserving shuffles, prose comparisons, original exploratory multiplicity, independent confirmation, authorial intent and decryption.

finding: The observed minimum is 128256. Of 49,999 within-section shuffle controls, 440 have a minimum no greater after searching the same 24 orders; plus-one estimate 0.00882.
limitations: Accounts only for the declared section-order search, not the earlier choice of word object, width or statistic. Cyclic classes and paired comparisons are not independent evidence. No intent or decryption claim; human review pending.
next_steps: The separate six-width comparison is published as lp1-width-selection; it does not combine width and section-order selection. Joint selection or sentence-preserving controls need explicit frozen procedures.

family.title: LP1 word lengths and column balance
